context.title: Box chart view
context.description: Visualizes the statistical distribution of results for a test, indicating the mean, the extremes, and various levels in between in a way that enables easy comparison between multiple data sets. A box chart displays key statistical information about each selected row in the test summary tab in a standard box plot elements. The upper border of the box indicates the 75%-line, the lower border the 25%-line, and the middle line the mean of the test. By default, the upper whisker indicates the 98%-line and the lower whisker the 2% line; this can be configured. Red dots indicate outlier values. The y-axis indicates the values to which each marker of a box corresponds; the x-axis lists the names of the test series represented by the boxes. The gray zones are the limits with which the test was executed. You can zoom in and out or adjust the appearance of the graph using the context menu.

context.description: Assign Var Here you either select an already defined variable for your For flow control node, or enter a new one. Assign Expr Here you assign the initial value by directly entering the value or by entering an expression. Condition Here you either select an already defined condition for your For flow control node, or enter a new one. Increment Var Here you select an already defined increment variable offset value, or enter the value directly. Increment Expr Here you enter the offset value that is used to increment the expression for the next execution of the same test suite within the loop. TestNum Inc In this box you enter the number by which the test number is to be incremented up when the flow control node is executed.

context.title: New 'If Node' wizard

Clicking the slash to the right of the Condition text box will open a list that contains all the condition variables defined for the testflow for selection if you wish. context.title: New 'Multi Bin Node' wizard

context.title: New 'New Run And Branch Node' wizard

topic.label: Inserting a 'Run and Branch Test Suite' node

context.title: New 'New Run Node' wizard
context.description: Here you insert a Run node test suite which allows the test to continue whether the device fails or not. By clicking on the check box to the left of the text box, you can select the parameters that you have defined for your test.

context.title: New 'Print Node' wizard
context.description: Enter a text or expression you want to see in the report window. This is only information and does not influence the test

context.title: New 'Print to Data Node' wizard

context.title: New 'Repeat Node' wizard
context.description: Condition Here you enter a condition for your "Repeat" flow control node. Clicking the slash to the right of the Condition text box will open a list that contains all the condition variables defined for the testflow for selection if you wish. TestNum Inc In this box you enter the number by which the test number is to be incremented up when the flow control node is executed.

context.title: New 'Special Test Suite' wizard
context.description: This window helps you to add a special test suite into the testflow.

context.title: New 'Stop Bin Node' wizard
context.description: The software and hardware bin numbers and names are arbitrary. The soft bins are virtual bins, used e.g. for statistical monitoring of production. One or more can be associated with a particular hardware bin. The hardware bin number and name defines the physical bin where the tested DUT ends up. Checking Reprobe will cause the DUT to be retested after binning. Checking Overon will allow the testflow to continue after a device fails.

topic.label: Inserting a good or bad Bin

context.title: New 'While Node' wizard

context.description: Visualizes the measured test values of dies on a wafer. The chart can be based on the maximum, mean, or minimum test values for each die. This is set in the preferences. A parametric wafer map displays the test measurements from each die in the selected row in the test summary tab. Each cell displays the result of the die at that location on the wafer. The two axes indicate the die coordinates. You can adjust the appearance of the graph using the context menu and the preferences.

context.title: Paste as new event

context.description: The Pattern Explorer lists all patterns of the loaded setup. Here you can create new patterns, new port bursts, new multiport bursts, or open them in their specific editors. You can also assign other pattern names, memory, wave tables, or pattern layouts.

context.title: Probability chart properties
context.description: Specify the labels and axis settings for a probability chart.

context.title: Probability chart view
context.description: Displays the probability that the test result for a given device does not exceed a certain value. You can also compare probability graphs from the same test suite, test method, and test. A probability chart displays the selected row from the test summary tab (or multiple rows, if all share the same test suite, test method, and test.) Each series of test results is represented by one line in the chart. The probability axis indicates how likely it is that a test results is equal to or less than the value indicated by the value axis. The gray zones are the limits with which the test was executed. You can zoom in and out or adjust the appearance of the graph using the context menu.

context.title: Probabilty chart preferences
context.description: Specify display options for all probability chart views.

context.title: Protocol Assignment Editor
context.description: With the protocol assignment editor you can assign your protocol ports to your protocol and a (hardware) pin resource to the protocol's pin role. Here you can assign pin roles of your protocol used for transactions to resource (hardware) pins of the V93000 test system.

context.title: Protocol Aware preferences
context.description: Select Enable alternate row coloring to display every second row of tables with a colored background. The default setting is: disabled. Select Automatically expand protocols node on related change to expand the protocol node in the Test Program Explorer upon loading or unloading a protocol. The default setting is: disabled.

context.title: Protocol editor - Level
context.description: Here you can define protocol specific level segments which can be mapped to the device level setup file. You can specify multiple level segments.

context.title: Protocol editor - Protocol Definition
context.description: The protocol editor is the central graphical user interface to define your protocol. It opens in the Protocol Definition tab per default. At protocol level you can create transactions and pin roles. If required you may define pin role groups and constant state character sequences. At transaction level you can define transaction length, parameters, symbols and encode/decode functions. At pin role level you can define pin role encode and decode functions or create new fields. At field level you can define field length, symbols and encode/decode functions.

context.title: Protocol editor - Timing
context.description: Here you can define protocol specific timing segments which can be mapped to the device timing setup file. You can specify multiple timing segments.

context.title: Protocol editor - Wavetable
context.description: Here you can define a unique protocol specific wafetable which can be mapped into the wavetable setup file. You can specify only one wavetable per protocol.

context.title: Protocol editor preferences
context.description: Here you can set the preferences for: Section Visibility Enable sections to have them extended in the corresponding detail page. If disabled, only the header of a section will be shown. Pin Role Editing and Pin Role Group Editing By disabling the event options On Delete, On Create and On Rename, the corresponding action will not be propagated as described.

context.title: Protocol Monitor
context.description: Displays a tabular overview of the results of one or more protocol monitor tests. Each row represents one PCI Express transaction. Transactions can be searched using the search field at the top of the view. Transaction details can be displayed by clicking the Show Properties toolbar button. Transaction sequences can be compared by clicking the Create Baseline toolbar button and the displaying the data to be compared.

context.title: Protocol Monitor preferences
context.description: Configure which columns are displayed in which order in Protocol Monitor views.

context.title: Search Configuration
context.description: All checked columns in this dialog are included in searches of the Protocol Monitor view and in comparisons when the compare mode is active. The Select All and Deselect All buttons provide shortcuts for checking or unchecking all columns.

context.title: Protocol Wrapper - select transactions
context.description: Select the transactions of your protocol which should be included into the wrapper class. Per default all transactions are included.

context.title: Protocol Wrapper Wizard
context.description: The wrapper generation wizard provides the possibility to generate your own C++ class from the protocol definition that can be used for test method programming. Enter the Class Name and Location where to store the generated files. Result Access Classes will be included to your wrapper class per default If you do not have generated result classes previously or modified your protocol definition, generate them by enabling the corresponding classes and enter a location for each.

context.title: Rata data view preferences
context.description: Specify the columns displayed in raw data views and their order.

context.title: Raw data view
context.description: Displays the individual data log records that make up the selected summary row in the data navigation view. Individual records can be excluded from evaluation by unchecking them in the checkmark column or by choosing Exclude from the context menu. The rows can be sorted by clicking the column titles and filtered by entering match conditions in the table filter (top row with blue background).

context.title: Remove a Sequence Block
context.description: To remove a sequence block, select a block you want to remove and right click Remove Sequence Block.

context.title: Rename Event
context.description: To rename the event together with all related test points, select the Update test points option (default). To rename the event only, but none of the test points, clear the Update test points check box. To exclude individual test points from renaming, click Next.

context.title: Rename Event

context.title: RF Analog Sequencing Group
context.description: Whenever an RF stimulus definition or measurement definition is created, a sequencer group is created for it automatically, and the sequencer group is updated automatically to reflect any subsequent changes in the definition.

context.title: RF Sequence Block View

context.title: RF Stimulus, Measurement Definition
context.description: To create an RF Stimulus or an RF Measurement Definition, right-Click in the RF Test Setup Browser and select New Stimulus Definition or New Measurement Definition.

context.title: RF Trace Verification
context.description: Trace Verification (TV) Calibration measures and calculates data at the same frequencies and on the same paths that are used during trace verification. Trace verification cannot be run until TV calibration has been run.

context.title: Sample Code
context.description: The Sample Code view is available for analog pins and RF definitions. It displays test method code for the pins in the Hardware View. You can copy and paste the code directly into your test method program. You can compare the sample code for a number of pins by opening several Sample Code views in parallel.

context.title: Sample Code
context.description: The Sample Code view provides code examples for controlling a measurement, stimulus, or any kind of data you can use as a starting point for your own test methods.

context.description: Here you can configure and save several layouts for a pattern. A layout defines which signals (equivalent to pins, pin aliases, and pin groups) are displayed and in which format they are displayed.

context.title: Save Partial As

context.title: Testflow Tool
context.description: Resolve name conflicts by adding suffix automatically If you enable this option, when pasting a node SmarTest adds a numeral suffix to the name. Otherwise it opens the Name Conflict window prompting you to enter a new name for the pasted node. Synchronize selection between Flow Data Editor and Flow Sequence Editor If you enable this option, the display of the test component is synchronized between the two editors. For example, if you click a test suite in the Flow Sequence Editor, the test suite is also in focus in the Flow Data Editor. Synchronize selection between Debug view and Testflow editors If you enable this option, when you execute the test suites one by one in the Debug view, the last executed test suite will be highlighted in the testflow tool. If you disable this option, the highlighted test suite in the testflow tool will not be changed with the execution in the Debug view. Execute selected UTM Test Method as separate process (to avoid blocking) Enabled SmarTest always executes the selected UTM Test Method on another executor as separate process. Beware that those executions do not share the same process space. The value of the global variable, for example, is different in each executor. Check UTM test method library version when opening testflow editor If you enable this option, when you open a testflow, the testflow tool will check whether the test method library is built on the version of SmarTest you are currently using. If not, a warning message will pop up. If you disable this option, no checking of the test method library will be done when you open a testflow. Pop up dialog window to configure whether or not to transfer the test suite to shmoo tool, when "Run Selected" shmoo test suite. If you enable this option, SmarTest opens a window asking you whether you want to transfer the test suite or not. If you disable this option, SmarTest transfers the test suite without further notice. Pop up dialog window to configure whether or not to copy those testflow variables existing only in the source testflow to the target testflow. If you enable this option, SmarTest opens a window asking you whether you want to create variables with their default value in the target testflow or not. If you disable this option, SmarTest creates the variables without further notice. Startup options Specify which editor (the Flow Data Editor or the Flow Sequence Editor) will be opened the next time you double-click the testflow item in the Test Program Explorer view.

context.title: Utility Line
context.description: The Utility Line View is part of the Hardware Perspective. It allows you to query the read and write states of utility pins and to set their write states. The task of the utility lines is to control electronic circuits on the DUT board such as relays, solenoids, indicators or similar external devices, or to read the state of devices mounted on the DUT board. Utility lines can be controlled by dedicated test functions, or by firmware commands and also by routing sets, or test method programs. You can group utility lines together with their control data. Such groups can be defined in the Pin Configuration Setup and are called Utility Purpose.
